2609.16933.title: When Confidence Signals Disagree: Local and Global Confidence in Autoregressive Language Models
2609.16933.paper_summary: Modern predictive systems expose multiple quantities that are commonly interpreted as measures of confidence. However, these quantities can summarize different aspects of the predictive process. This distinction matters when confidence is used to evaluate reliability or inform downstream oversight and control. We investigate whether different confidence readouts are empirically interchangeable in an autoregressive language model by comparing local confidence, defined from the probability of the greedy-selected answer token, with global confidence, defined from modal-answer frequency under repeated sampling. Across MMLU and ARC Challenge, the two signals are weakly correlated and differ substantially in their association with correctness: global confidence is moderately associated with correctness, whereas local confidence shows little association. We further test whether question-level disagreement between the signals is associated with sampling instability. On ARC, larger local--global confidence gaps are associated with higher answer entropy, more distinct sampled answers, and lower modal-answer concentration. The gap--entropy association persists when disagreement and instability are estimated from disjoint stochastic samples, indicating that it is not explained by shared finite-sample variation. The corresponding relationship is substantially weaker on MMLU, where only 4% of questions exhibit sampling instability. These results show that confidence readouts derived from the same predictive system are not empirically interchangeable and that their disagreement can provide a diagnostic of unstable sampling behavior. Confidence should therefore be treated as an explicitly defined measurement rather than as a single intrinsic scalar property of a model, particularly when it is used to inform downstream evaluation, oversight, or control.
2609.16933.paper_summary_zh: 現代的預測系統揭示了多個量度，這些量度通常被解釋為信心的指標。<lb/>然而，這些量度可以總結預測過程的不同方面。<lb/>當信心被用來評估可靠性或提供下游監督和控制時，這一區別是重要的。<lb/>我們通過比較本地信心（從貪婪選擇的答案標記的概率定義）和全局信心（從重複抽樣下的模式答案頻率定義）來調查不同的信心讀數在自回歸語言模型中是否可以互換。<lb/>在 MMLU 和 ARC 挑戰中，這兩種信號的相關性較弱，並且在與正確性關聯方面有顯著差異：全局信心與正確性中度相關，而本地信心則幾乎沒有相關性。<lb/>我們進一步測試信號之間的問題級別不一致是否與抽樣不穩定性相關。<lb/>在 ARC 中，較大的本地-全局信心差距與較高的答案熵、更多不同的抽樣答案以及較低的模式答案集中度相關。<lb/>當不一致性和不穩定性是從不相交的隨機樣本中估計時，差距-熵的關聯仍然存在，這表明它並不是由共享的有限樣本變異解釋的。<lb/>在 MMLU 上，對應的關係顯著較弱，只有 4% 的問題顯示出抽樣不穩定性。<lb/>這些結果表明，來自同一預測系統的信心讀數在實證上並不可互換，且它們的不一致性可以提供不穩定抽樣行為的診斷。<lb/>因此，信心應被視為明確定義的測量，而不是模型的單一內在標量屬性，特別是當它用來通知下游評估、監督或控制時。
